sections.title: What the named products describe
paragraphs:
Netic’s company page positions its work around enterprises in essential-service industries. That positioning does not establish a minimum company size or prove that a smaller contractor is ineligible. Confirm the commercial fit directly. [Netic company](https://www.netic.ai/company)

### Convert: existing inbound demand

Convert describes incoming calls, texts, web widgets and third-party sources. Its published scope includes booking and rescheduling, with jobs entering a CRM or field-service system, plus a Customer Hub for staff handling. Those descriptions do not identify every supported connector or account permission. Ask for the exact destination and actions in your proposal. [Netic Convert](https://www.netic.ai/convert)

### Cultivate: customer outreach

Cultivate describes autonomous campaigns for activities such as maintenance and membership renewal, using customer and other data. That is outbound engagement, a separate authority decision from responding to someone who calls your office. Determine the proposed audience, trigger, channel and approval process before enabling any campaign. This guide does not establish legal compliance or authorize outreach. [Netic Cultivate](https://www.netic.ai/cultivate)

### Evaluate: human-call assessment and recovery

Evaluate describes scoring calls handled by human customer-service staff against business-defined criteria. Its page also describes re-engaging leads after calls that fall below the selected quality bar. Treat assessment and subsequent customer contact as separate actions to include or exclude explicitly. A low score is not, by itself, an instruction from your business to contact the customer. [Netic Evaluate](https://www.netic.ai/evaluate)

### Empower: operational analysis

Empower describes operational views and analysis by customer, geography or campaign. Ask which underlying records support the view you plan to use. A dashboard summary should not replace the authoritative appointment or job record when the office needs to establish that work was booked. [Netic Empower](https://www.netic.ai/empower)

sections.title: A proposal boundary matrix
paragraphs:
The product purposes below come from the cited pages. The remaining columns are original purchasing questions, not confirmed package inclusions. A site navigation link does not establish a separately purchasable module, a bundled price or permission to run the associated workflow.

| Workstream | Initiating event to specify | Customer-facing action to approve | Data and office owner to identify | Proof to request | Explicit exclusion to consider |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Convert | Incoming inquiry | Answer, record a request, make a supported booking or hand off | Destination system; scheduling/customer-service owner | Actual proposed booking or request record | Outbound campaigns not included merely because inbound answering is selected |
| Cultivate | Approved campaign trigger | Proposed message or call and reply handling | Authorized audience data; campaign owner | Trigger, audience, content and reply destination | No campaign outside the agreed audience and purpose |
| Evaluate | Human CSR interaction selected for assessment | None for scoring alone; any follow-up separately approved | Authorized review evidence; quality owner | Scoring criteria and traceable supporting interaction | No automatic recovery contact solely from a score unless expressly agreed |
| Empower | Data available for analysis | Usually an internal view; confirm any attached action | Defined source records; reporting owner | Reconciliation of a sample result to its source | No assumption that a displayed outcome proves a completed job |

Add a final column to the actual quote for **included, optional, excluded or unresolved**. Have the seller fill it for the proposed arrangement. Do not infer that all four workstreams are included because they appear together on the website.

sections.title: Follow one fictional customer through three separate events
paragraphs:
Use this original proposal demonstration with invented data and the provider’s permission. It has not been run against Netic. The point is to reveal boundaries between workstreams without treating a product suite as one undifferentiated automation.

**Customer `DEMO-NETIC-01` first makes an inbound inquiry.** The caller asks for an approved service. Record the inbound interaction ID, the selected customer/location and the resulting appointment or request. If the office must still approve the work, keep that status visible. This checks the Convert scope you intend to buy.

**Later, the same fictional customer replies to a membership campaign.** Only include this step if outbound work is within the proposed scope. Record a separate campaign ID, the authorized trigger and the reply’s destination. Ask who stops or changes the campaign when the customer’s situation changes. Do not reuse the inbound-call record as evidence that the customer was eligible for outreach.

**A human CSR subsequently handles a call.** If Evaluate is included, ask for the relevant criteria and supporting evidence. If a low score could trigger recovery activity, show the separate approval or configured authority for that action. An assessment result and a follow-up operation should remain distinguishable in the office’s records.

| Record to inspect | Identifier / evidence | Responsible office role | Actual result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inbound request and booking outcome | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Campaign authority, trigger and customer reply | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Human-call evaluation and any separately authorized follow-up | ___ | ___ | ___ |

Leave results blank until the demonstration occurs. If you are buying inbound answering only, mark the other events excluded. The purpose is a clear boundary, not a reason to purchase more features.

sections.title: Ask for a scoped quote, not an assumed receptionist rate
paragraphs:
No current amount or universal billing unit was established from the official pages reviewed. Ask the provider to quote your actual workstreams, software and operating arrangement. That evidence gap is not a claim that Netic never publishes prices.

Request written terms for:

- Included products and any optional workstreams.
- The billing unit, allowances, implementation charges and treatment of additional usage.
- The named CRM or field-service destination and supported actions.
- Which data the selected work requires and who grants access.
- Staff responsibilities for operating rules, campaign approval and review findings.
- Monitoring, support, change requests and the process for ending the arrangement.

Keep the commercial and authority questions together. A product may be priced in the proposal yet still need your business to approve particular actions before use. Conversely, leaving a workflow unpriced does not make it free or included.

sections.title: When this evaluation belongs on your shortlist
paragraphs:
Netic warrants a closer product-scope review when your business is considering a broader customer-operation platform, particularly where inbound handling, staff workflows and customer engagement need to be evaluated together. That is a fit assessment based on its documented positioning, not a claim about results or an endorsement of autonomous operation without oversight.

For an AI answering option, [review Revo](https://www.revoapp.ai/) and confirm its selected plan and supported setup. sections.title: Compare calls with minutes
paragraphs:
SkipCalls’ fair-use page states 200 calls per month for Starter and 350 for PRO. It says call length does not change the call count, excludes unwanted spam from fair usage, and describes seasonal peaks as acceptable. For consistently higher usage, it describes contacting the customer about a more suitable plan rather than automatic cutoff or surprise charges. These are policy statements, not an independently verified billing result. [SkipCalls fair-use policy](https://skipcalls.com/fair-usage)

That gives an office a different planning unit from minutes. Count ordinary new inquiries, existing-customer calls and follow-ups separately when describing your workload to the seller. Do not convert a call allowance into a guaranteed number of minutes by multiplying it by a guessed average duration.

Ask what “consistently” means for your account and what written terms would apply if your volume grows. A policy allowing a seasonal peak is not evidence that sustained volume of any size is included at the same price.

paragraphs:
A usage alert and a stop condition serve different purposes. HighLevel's usage-limit documentation describes both continued operation with notifications and blocking at a configured limit. Confirm which setting applies to the proposed subaccount, who can change it and what a caller-facing workflow does if AI pauses. This article does not verify actual account enforcement or establish a ceiling on the entire phone bill. [AI Usage Limits](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007813-ai-usage-limits).

2. Which components are included in the customer price, and which are separately metered?
3. Who owns configuration, support, charge review and additional-usage approval?
4. What will a representative authorized inquiry produce: a message, a pending request or a confirmed booking in the agreed destination?
5. What happens if the workflow pauses, the office cannot accept the request or a connection fails?

If your business already uses HighLevel, compare the incremental configured cost and remaining office work. If you only need call answering, compare a narrower answering service against the same required tasks—not against the price of an entire platform serving other purposes.
